{"result":"# The Rust Programming Language and Memory Safety

## Introduction

Rust is a general-purpose, multi-paradigm language that emphasizes performance, type safety, concurrency, and memory safety [1][2]. Of these goals, memory safety is central to its design [2].

## Origins

Graydon Hoare started Rust in 2006, and Mozilla Research sponsored it from 2009 [2]. It was first publicly released in 2010, and version 1.0 followed in 2015 [2].

## Design Influences

Rust borrows ideas from functional programming, including immutability, algebraic data types, and pattern matching [1]. Its syntax is similar to C++ [2].

## Memory Safety Explained

Memory safety protects programs from bugs such as buffer overflows and dangling pointers [3]. Rust guarantees memory safety without needing a garbage collector [2].

## Comparing Approaches

Java is memory-safe because its runtime checks array bounds [3]. C, C++, and Fortran allow arbitrary pointer arithmetic without bounds checking, which makes them memory-unsafe [3].

## Conclusion
